slides.subline: Anthracite Coffee, Hapjeong — open since 2009 inside a disused shoe factory

slides.label: The year Anthracite opened inside an abandoned shoe factory in Hapjeong — and kept the factory
slides.note: Sources: Kinfolk · Sprudge Coffee · Seoul Metropolitan Government official tourism site (english.visitseoul.net)

items.d: The original shell was kept rather than stripped out and restyled
The line the factory ran shoes along is now the hand-drip bar
Beans are roasted in-house; a resident pastry chef bakes on site

slides.title:
Nothing here was
made to look old.
slides.body:
Seoul's cafe boom usually works the other way round — a room is gutted, then dressed back up in industrial style. Anthracite's first branch skipped the middle step. It moved into a shoe factory in Hapjeong in 2009 and left the concrete, the stone floor and the beams where they were, which is why the pour-over bar is a piece of the old production line.

The menu carries the same idea. Roasts are named after writers and artists, so an order can come out as a Natsume Soseki or a Pablo Neruda rather than a number.

items.d: Hapjeong, Mapo-gu — this is the original branch, and the one the rest grew out of
Listings show no regular closing day — worth confirming before a long trip over
Cakes, madeleines and financiers are baked in-house alongside the coffee

caption:
A Seoul cafe that moved into a shoe factory and left the factory where it was.

Anthracite Coffee, Hapjeong: open since 2009 on Tojeong-ro 5-gil, with roasts named after writers and a hand-drip bar made from the old conveyor line.

Hours change, so it's worth checking before you go.
